script.stored_text_completeness: All 17825 canonical characters read sequentially in full in 1 bounded ranges; auto-generated untimed text; stored text ends on "Don't let that be the end of the story." with no sign-off; two sentences end mid-thought ("Americans seem to instinctively", "wondering how"); the 55-64 median is given as $320,700 then $364,500; Derek's salary shifts between $115,000 combined, $75,000 and $82,000 across benchmarks; audio, timed delivery and editing unverified.
script.opening_words: You're sitting at the dinner table with your college friends, the ones you haven't seen in 2 years because everyone's busy now, and somehow the conversation drifts, the way it always does after the second bottle of wine, toward money. Not in a serious way, just someone casually mentioning they refinanced, someone else saying they maxed out their Roth this year, and then one guy, the one who became an engineer and married someone in pharma, says, almost as an
script.ending_words: written right now in the decision about this year's raise and whether you finally set up that Roth, in whether you run the real numbers instead of the comfortable ones. None of it feels important in the moment. All of it is. By watching this, you just did something most people never do. You looked the real numbers in the eye. Don't let that be the end of the story.
script.analysis: Full 17825 canonical characters read. A single-narrator data explainer with a composite (Derek): hook (friends near "the number"), mean vs median and wealth concentration, SCF medians by age with Fidelity benchmarks, lifestyle inflation, car and student debt, the emotional experience, homeowner vs renter gap, auto-enrolment, generational comparisons and the wealth transfer, decade-by-decade actions (start, max, catch-ups, super catch-up, Social Security), Derek's catch-up plan and Ramsey close. Core data are accurate; the 55-64 median and Derek's salary are inconsistent within the video.
beat_map: How the machine works: raises, cars, student loans.
